decisions.rationale: The passage reports only within-group changes for this contrast (significant 1RM decrease in VES, none stated for PLB) and no between-group test of VES vs PLB, so a 'no detectable between-group difference' claim is not supported; the quote if anything hints at a decrease.

Both trained arms (PLB+RT and VES+RT) showed significant 1RM increases and no between-group difference between the two trained arms is reported, consistent with no_effect of the supplement on the training adaptation.
Quote explicitly states AS group had higher increases in arm lean mass (0.96 vs 0.59 kg, P=.003) than PLA, directly supporting an increase relative to placebo plus training.
Quote reports greater increase in skeletal muscle mass index in AS vs PLA (0.71 vs 0.42 kg/m², P=.004), supporting increase relative to the placebo-training comparator.
Quote reports larger handgrip strength gain in AS vs PLA (3.66 vs 1.16 kg, P=.047), supporting a larger training adaptation with supplementation.
Quote reports greater knee extension strength gain in AS vs PLA (2.28 vs 1.02 kg, P<.001), directly supporting increase.

The quote describes only the effect of aerobic training on VO2 measures, with no between-group comparison involving the stated supplemented sedentary comparator; it is also ambiguous which aerobic measure this finding refers to.

The statement that training increased VO2 TVE is a training effect, not a supplement-versus-comparator contrast; no between-group difference relative to the AS sedentary group is reported in the passage.

The passage concludes shortened P3 latencies resulted from exercise training 'instead of vitamin E usage', with both E and EV groups improving, supporting no additional effect of vitamin E versus training alone.
Quote states peak-to-peak amplitude values were unaltered in all groups, supporting no between-group difference for the supplemented arm.
Quote states neither exercise nor vitamin E altered plasma TAC, directly supporting no_effect of supplementation relative to exercise alone.
Quote explicitly reports no statistical difference in aerobic capacity between supplement and placebo groups at season end.
Quote explicitly reports no statistical difference in strength between S and PL groups at season end.
Quote explicitly reports no statistical difference in speed (sprint performance) between S and PL groups at season end.

Only a within-group paired t test in the vitamin group is reported; no comparison with the placebo group is given, so a smaller adaptation relative to the comparator cannot be verified from this passage.
The quote reports an intergroup (between-group) comparison showing significantly decreased creatine kinase in group 1, the supplemented arm, supporting the decrease direction.
Quote reports GPx1 declines in both vitamin and placebo groups 'with no effects of supplementation', supporting no between-group difference.
Quote states no changes were observed for muscle mnSOD, consistent with no detectable between-group supplementation effect.
Quote states no changes were observed for muscle GSH, supporting no_effect relative to placebo.
Quote reports similar αB-crystallin decreases in both groups explicitly 'with no effects of supplementation'.
Quote reports comparable HSP27 decreases in both groups with 'no effects of supplementation', supporting no_effect.
Quote reports a significant decrease in uric acid in the vitamin group (−24%) compared with placebo (+6%, P<0.001), supporting the decrease direction.
Quote states plasma GSH increased in both groups with no effect of supplementation, supporting no between-group difference.
Quote states TAS did not change after training or supplementation, supporting no_effect.
The quote reports only a significant group×time interaction without direction or which group changed, so a decrease relative to placebo cannot be verified.
Quote reports the primary endurance outcome Qend showed no additional increase in the antioxidant group (p=0.56), supporting no_effect versus placebo.
Quote reports a significant between-group difference in QMVC in favor of antioxidant supplementation (p<0.001), supporting increase.
Quote states no significant VO2max changes in either group, supporting no detectable between-group difference relative to placebo plus training.

Prompt version: `quote-verification-v1`

Independently assess whether each supplied source passage supports its proposed measured direction
